## A sixth pair, minted after this card was filed — 5 of 7 now

PR **#13923** (card **#13762**) was opened at 17:04:52Z, roughly half an hour after this card was filed. Measured at 17:1xZ:

| carrier | `needs:contract-review` |
|:--|:--|
| PR #13923 | ✅ |
| card #13762 | ❌ (labels were `documentation`, `pm:dispatched`, `domain:engine`, `priority:p3`) |

Synced by hand, like the four before it. Running tally on this board today: **5 of 7 measured pairs were out of sync at the moment a human looked.**

⚠️ This one is worth recording separately, because it is **not** the same failure as the other four — it is the opposite direction, and it argues the same conclusion from the other side.

PR #13923's own body declares, verbatim:

> - **Path limb — NO.** … It does not touch `packages/spec/src/`.
> - **Content limb — NO.** Comment-only in the `.ts` file … No accept/reject behaviour changes and no published surface widens.
>
> Both limbs read NO. The `needs:contract-review` label is attached anyway, **per the unconditional label requirement in the dispatch**.

⇒ So the label went onto that PR **because a dispatch order said to attach it unconditionally**, not because the gate's own predicate fired — while the card, which the gate actually reads for the declaration limb, got nothing.

That is the same defect this card describes, seen from the other end: **the label's presence and the gate's predicate are independent variables.** Four times today it was hung by the predicate and missed on a carrier; here it was hung by an instruction on a PR the predicate says it does not apply to. Either way, reading the label tells you almost nothing about whether a contract question is live — which is precisely what the **重挂前先查裁决** recovery rule assumes it does.

⚠️ And it interacts with **⛔ 不预挂** (maintainer, 2026-08-28: never attach before a reviewable increment exists). Attaching unconditionally is not *pre*-hanging — the increment exists — but it is over-hanging, and it costs a review round on a three-file comment-only diff. Whether "attach unconditionally" is actually the standing rule or a dispatch-local instruction is a question this card's remedy should settle rather than inherit; the review now running on #13923 has been asked to quote the governing text either way.

⛔ No re-grade, no option chosen — recording the instance while it is fresh.

Sample evidence in the thread to take as given: 3/3 strip-then-ship timeline (comments 5461595204/5461677786/5462161173) and the 5-of-7 tally (5481873509). The #12902 tool-face constraint (PRs could not be labeled) is contradicted by today's board (5 of 6 PRs carry the label) — re-verify which write channel works rather than inheriting either claim.
